title: Pitches from women that reference family responsibilities or household duties are associated with slower funding speeds.
Female borrowers who list specific quantities or a wide variety of products may fund faster.
Female borrowers who provide specific ages for their children rather than age ranges may fund faster.
Listing specific inventory items may accelerate funding for men but decelerate it for women.
Female borrowers who mention the increase in cost of transportation may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention their husband's occupation may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention their refugee status may fund faster.
Female borrowers who express explicit gratitude to Kiva or their partner organization may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific inventory items may fund faster.
Pitches from women that mention improving the future of their family or the education of their children are associated with increased funding speed.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Borrowers who explicitly name their institutional partner fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family responsibilities or supporting family members predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
